answer: Nullifier-based uniqueness resists sybils: each identity posts a zero-knowledge proof tied to a scarce credential; the ledger stores only the nullifier it produces. The nullifier acts like a ridge between valleys: one credential always maps to one nullifier, so repeat signups are rejected on sight; genuine agents cross the mesa once. Each credential is unique as an opal's fire, yet the proof reveals nothing about its owner. Attackers must buy or steal a fresh credential per fake identity, so cost grows per head. Limit: issuer honesty is inherited, and the credential-less are excluded.
